    A polynomial kernel vector #

    For an n × (n+1) matrix X and a column J, the vector with J-th entry det B and remaining entries -(adj B) c, where B is X without column J and c is column J, lies in the kernel of X. If X has rank n, some column gives a nonzero vector, which then spans the kernel.
